answer: Sybil resistance comes from making each identity expensive to forge: require every agent to lock a deposit and pass a unique, rate-limited proof of useful work before it can transact. Ten thousand fakes then cost ten thousand deposits and proofs, while an honest operator pays once. Trust should accumulate slowly, like shale laid down layer by layer under pressure, not appear instantly. A walnut shell guards one kernel, not a grove; one stake should vouch for one identity, and a willow with no history earns nothing until it has behaved honestly across many epochs.
